deep.reconstruction:
Context and purpose. The heading reads 'Beweis des Reciprocitätsgesetzes unter den Resten und Nichtresten, deren Grad eine Primzahl ist' ('Proof of the reciprocity law among residues and non-residues whose degree is a prime number'). This nearly reproduces the title of Kummer's memoir 'Über die allgemeinen Reciprocitätsgesetze unter den Resten und Nichtresten der Potenzen, deren Grad eine Primzahl ist' (Abh. Berlin 1859; announced 1850). The page is therefore a set of working or reading notes on Kummer's lambda-th power reciprocity in the cyclotomic integers Z[alpha], with alpha^lambda = 1 and lambda an odd prime.

The second line, with a crossed-out first word, reads roughly '... of the general Legendre symbol and of the index ind(phi(alpha), mod psi(alpha))'. It announces the link between the power-residue symbol and Kummer's index: (psi/theta) = alpha^{ind}, where psi^{(N theta - 1)/lambda} ≡ alpha^{ind} mod theta. The third line ('Bestimmende complexe Größe - Sigma(c) ...') is too abbreviated to reconstruct with certainty.

(A) Normal form of a quotient. Let psi(alpha) and phi(alpha) be two cyclotomic integers 'of the same class'. Most probably this means the same residue class with respect to powers of (1-alpha), as in Kummer's primary numbers (my interpretation). Riemann asserts that psi/phi can be written as
  (c_0 + c_1 alpha + ... + c_{lambda-1} alpha^{lambda-1})/(1-alpha)^2 - (Sum c_nu)/(1-alpha)^2 + (Sum nu c_nu)/(1-alpha) + (an integer).
The structural content (my filling) is the Taylor expansion at alpha = 1. For c(alpha) = Sum c_nu alpha^nu we have
  c(alpha) = c(1) - (1-alpha) c'(1) + (1-alpha)^2 * (integer polynomial), with c'(1) = Sum nu c_nu.
Hence [c(alpha) - Sum c + (1-alpha) Sum nu c]/(1-alpha)^2 is integral. So the displayed expression is the polar part of c(alpha)/(1-alpha)^2 at alpha = 1 removed, plus an integer. The letters 'a' in the image are the same coefficients as the c's.

(B) Euler criterion for a general modulus chi(alpha). Let Phi(chi) be the number of residues in a complete residue system mod chi that are prime to chi; this is the generalized Euler totient, equal to the order of (Z[alpha]/chi)^*. Let psi be prime to chi.

(B1) Riemann first writes psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} ≡ alpha^{Sum mu} mod chi as a general statement. Here Sum mu is an exponent left unspecified.

(B2) Case 1: chi has (at least two) distinct prime factors. Then psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} ≡ 1 modulo each prime-power factor, hence ≡ 1 mod chi.
- Implicit step (mine): Phi is multiplicative.
- Each factor Phi(theta_i^{m_i}) is divisible by lambda, because N theta_i ≡ 1 mod lambda.
- So Phi(chi)/lambda is still a multiple of every Phi(theta_i^{m_i}).
- Euler-Fermat in each (Z[alpha]/theta_i^{m_i})^* then gives ≡ 1, and CRT gives ≡ 1 mod chi.

(B3) Case 2: chi = theta^m with theta prime (prime to lambda).
- Phi(chi) = N(theta)^{m-1}(N theta - 1).
- Since N theta ≡ 1 mod lambda, the exponent Phi/lambda = N theta^{m-1} * (N theta - 1)/lambda is an integer.
- Conclusion: psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} ≡ alpha^{ind(psi, mod theta)} = (psi/theta) mod chi.
- Implicit justification (mine), step 1: x = psi^{Phi/lambda} satisfies x^lambda ≡ 1 mod theta^m. Because lambda is prime to theta and the alpha^k are distinct mod theta, the only solutions of x^lambda ≡ 1 mod theta^m are the alpha^k (Hensel lifting).
- Step 2: mod theta, the Frobenius relation psi^{N theta} ≡ psi gives psi^{N theta^{m-1}(N theta - 1)/lambda} ≡ psi^{(N theta - 1)/lambda} ≡ alpha^{ind}.
- So the congruence holds mod theta^m, not merely mod theta. Riemann first wrote 'mod chi' after the index, struck it, and then put 'mod chi' at the end.

The upshot: the Euler-type power psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} reproduces the residue symbol only for prime-power moduli. For moduli with several primes it is trivially 1. So a Jacobi-type generalized symbol must be defined multiplicatively, not via an Euler criterion.

(C) Last line. 'We split these sums into partial sums, collecting in one partial sum all terms for which nu has the same greatest common divisor with m.' This is the standard decomposition of a sum over residues nu mod m by d = gcd(nu, m). It is presumably preparation for a Gauss-lemma / Eisenstein-type evaluation of the exponent Sum mu. It is not carried out on this page.
errors: The general assertion psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} ≡ alpha^{Sum mu} mod chi is stated without defining Sum mu. The page itself shows it is trivially 1 when chi has two distinct prime factors, so as a general statement it is only a placeholder.

Hypotheses are implicit: psi must be prime to chi, and the prime factors theta of chi must be prime to lambda (needed both for N theta ≡ 1 mod lambda and for Hensel lifting of the lambda-th roots of unity).
In case B2, 'verschiedene Primfactoren' must mean at least two distinct prime factors. The step needs lambda dividing each Phi(theta_i^{m_i}); this is true, but it is not stated.

In case B3, the passage from the congruence mod theta to mod theta^m (via uniqueness of lambda-th roots of unity mod theta^m) is not justified on the page. The struck 'mod chi' suggests Riemann hesitated here.
In (A), the meaning of 'zu derselben Klasse gehörige' is not specified, so the claim about psi/phi cannot be fully checked. The underlying Taylor identity at alpha = 1 is correct.

results.what: Normal form: a cyclotomic quotient written as c(alpha)/(1-alpha)^2 minus its polar part at alpha = 1, i.e. [c(alpha) - c(1) + (1-alpha) Sum nu c_nu]/(1-alpha)^2, is integral, up to an added integer.
results.modern_name: Expansion in the uniformizer (1-alpha) at the prime above lambda; primary-number normalization
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1840s-1850s, primary numbers and the (1-alpha)-adic expansions)

results.what: psi^{Phi(chi)/lambda} ≡ 1 mod chi when chi has at least two distinct prime factors.
results.modern_name: Euler criterion fails for composite moduli (lambda-th power analogue of a^{phi(n)/2} ≡ 1 mod n for n with two odd prime factors)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss/Euler for lambda = 2; Kummer for cyclotomic integers

results.what: For chi = theta^m: Phi(theta^m) = N theta^{m-1}(N theta - 1) and psi^{Phi/lambda} ≡ alpha^{ind_theta psi} = (psi/theta) mod theta^m.
results.modern_name: Euler's criterion for the lambda-th power residue symbol (generalized to prime-power moduli)
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1850, 1859), building on Jacobi and Eisenstein

results.what: Decomposition of a sum over residues nu mod m into partial sums by gcd(nu, m).

deep.surprise_reason: These are reading or working notes on Kummer's higher reciprocity programme; the title almost copies Kummer's 1859 memoir. All mathematics shown is standard Kummer-era material (generalized Euler criterion, totient of prime powers, power-residue symbol via the index). It is mildly interesting as documentation that Riemann worked through Kummer's lambda-th power reciprocity, which is not a well-known part of his Nachlass, but it contains no new result.

checkable.sympy: x,c0,c1,c2,c3,c4=symbols('x c0 c1 c2 c3 c4'); c=c0+c1*x+c2*x**2+c3*x**3+c4*x**4; rem(expand(c - c.subs(x,1) + (1-x)*diff(c,x).subs(x,1)), (1-x)**2, x) == 0
checkable.asserts: c(alpha) - c(1) + (1-alpha)*Sum nu c_nu is divisible by (1-alpha)^2, so the expression in (A) is integral.

checkable.sympy: all(pow(a, totient(5*13)//2, 5*13)==1 for a in range(1,65) if gcd(a,65)==1)
checkable.asserts: Rational analogue (lambda = 2) of case B2: a^{phi(n)/lambda} ≡ 1 mod n when n has two distinct prime factors.

checkable.sympy: p=7; lam=3; m=3; all((pow(a, totient(p**m)//lam, p**m) - pow(a,(p-1)//lam,p)) % p == 0 for a in range(1,p**m) if a%p!=0)
checkable.asserts: Rational analogue of B3 (N theta = p ≡ 1 mod lambda): a^{p^{m-1}(p-1)/lambda} ≡ a^{(p-1)/lambda} mod p, i.e. the power residue symbol.

checkable.sympy: p=7; lam=3; m=3; all(pow(pow(a, totient(p**m)//lam, p**m), lam, p**m)==1 for a in range(1,p**m) if a%p!=0) and len(set(pow(a, totient(p**m)//lam, p**m) for a in range(1,p**m) if a%p!=0))==lam
checkable.asserts: psi^{Phi(theta^m)/lambda} is always one of exactly lambda roots of unity mod theta^m (Hensel lifting), so the congruence holds mod theta^m.
Phi(theta^m) = N theta^{m-1}(N theta - 1) in the rational case.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the first word is struck out; the rest reads '... d. allgem. Legendre'schen Zeichen und des Ind. ind(phi(alpha), mod psi(alpha))'. The letters in the index argument may be swapped (ind(psi, mod phi)); the reading is uncertain.

In the displayed normal form the coefficient letters written 'a' in 'Sigma a/(1-alpha)^2' and 'Sigma a nu/(1-alpha)' are the c_nu of the numerator. Mathematically the expression is [c(alpha) - Sigma c_nu]/(1-alpha)^2 + Sigma nu c_nu/(1-alpha) + integer.

In 'psi(alpha)^{Phi/lambda} ≡ alpha^{ind(psi(alpha), mod theta(alpha))}' the struck text after the exponent is 'mod chi(alpha)'; the final 'mod chi(alpha)' after the symbol (psi/theta) is the retained one.
The phrase before 'Potenz einer Primzahl' is a struck 'eine' (or 'die'); 'Ist chi(alpha) Potenz einer Primzahl theta(alpha)' is the intended reading.
Line 'Enthält chi(alpha) verschiedene Primfactoren': the first word appears overwritten/struck and rewritten, and 'mod chi(alpha)' continues on the next line.
